subject: Fwd: Short extension for Lab POC - top-up vs credits
messages:
From: James Adler <jadler@lumos.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lumos.ai Procurement <procurement@lumos.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Short extension for Lab POC - options

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the help during the last week of the Lab POC — the model throughput improvements were promising. We need a brief runway to finish our additional integration tests and a short set of user acceptance trials. Would Redwood be able to extend the POC by 3 weeks?

Two things we'd like to understand:
- Option A: a timebox top-up (one-off purchase) that buys us another 3 weeks of equivalent capacity.
- Option B: a small credits bucket that we can draw from (pay-as-you-go style) that covers variable usage during those 3 weeks.

From your side, can you:
1) Share pricing for both options (showing list price and a partner/discounted rate if available)
2) Confirm whether a PO or DocuSign amendment is required to extend the trial
3) Outline any limitations on model variants or concurrency for the extended period

We have an internal procurement window that closes Nov 18; ideally we can get final terms and a link to sign before then. I attached the current SOW for reference.

Appreciate the help — we want to accelerate to a conversion decision quickly.

Best,
James
---
Attachment: LumOS_SOW_v1.pdf (application/pdf, 128 KB)
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>

Cc: Lumos.ai Procurement <procurement@lumos.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Short extension for Lab POC - options

Hi James — great to hear the throughput gains were useful. We can definitely bridge you for three weeks. Two practical routes below (I've included the high-level economics so you can share with procurement):

Option 1 — Timebox top-up (simpler for procurement):
- 3-week top-up covering the existing reserved capacity profile
- List price: $12,000 for 3 weeks
- Preferred term price (10% off): $10,800
- Delivery: one-time invoice + DocuSign amendment to the SOW
- Limitations: pins to the current model/instance profile; burst beyond profile billed at pay-as-you-go

Option 2 — Credits bucket (flexible):
- $8,000 credits loaded into your account, usable across models and concurrency
- Recommended if you expect variable spike behavior during UAT
- Credits expire 30 days from issuance

Quick notes: we can also do a small discretionary concession — a one-time $1,200 onboarding credit if you sign before Nov 18 (effectively increasing the credits bucket or reducing the top-up net cost).

Next steps I suggest:
- You confirm preference A/B
- If A, I’ll route a DocuSign amendment and request procurement PO details
- If B, we can issue the credits once we have a signed MSA addendum or an internal PO with the charge code

Looping in your tech contact on the cadence we saw in logs — happy to provide a short ops note if you want to pin down concurrency headroom.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference

Ask: can we approve a one-time concession up to $1,500 (or a straight 12.5% discount on the top-up) to keep the deal moving? Risk: Lumos is evaluating two vendors and procurement will likely compare final out-of-pocket cost.

If approved I will proceed with DocuSign amendment and request their PO. If you'd prefer, we can flip to a credits structure which preserves list price but trades revenue shape.

Thanks Naomi — good, straightforward ask. Approve the following:

- Offer the 3-week timebox top-up at $10,800 (10% preferred rate) and include a $1,200 onboarding credit applied as a post-signing invoice credit (net economics equivalent to ~20% off list for this short bridge).
- If they insist on credits instead, we price the credits bucket at $8,000 and do not apply the $1,200 credit (credits preserve revenue recognition).
- No additional concessions beyond the $1,200 onboarding credit without legal sign-off.

Please proceed to generate the DocuSign amendment (use DocuSign_Lumos_PO.pdf template), request a procurement PO, and add the HubSpot note under DEAL-937. I'll notify Finance to expect a short-term invoice.
